Date: 2026-02-26T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on performance targets

Thanks for the call earlier, Marissa — good to meet the team. Per our discussion, here are the performance targets EdgeFin cares about for the pilot: 
- 99th percentile latency (token-to-token streaming): <= 120ms for 512-token average responses
- Tail latency (99.9th): <= 250ms
- Sustained throughput: 250 reqs/min with concurrency of 12 (burst to 30)
- Streaming support required (server-sent partial tokens + early stop)

We'd like a reproducible benchmark so we can compare apples-to-apples between Redwood and our current provider. I attached a small prompt sample to start (edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json). Can you confirm Redwood's benchmark methodology and what we'll measure? Also please include how you handle cold-start vs warm KV cache during the run.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Platform
EdgeFin

Hi Sam — leaving a few technical notes here so we are explicit about methodology and reproducibility. Quick bullets: 

Measurement definitions:
- Token-level streaming latency = time between Redwood emitting token N and client receiving token N (measured by runner using keep-alive SSE socket).
- Request latency (end-to-end) = time from HTTP request start to final token received.
- We will report p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 and provide full histograms (CSV).

Warm vs cold:
- Cold run: service process restarted, model weights loaded, KV cache empty, single-shot ramp to target QPS; we run 3 cold trials and report medians.
- Warm run: runner warms the model with continuous traffic for 10 minutes, then we collect a 15-minute steady-state window.

Throughput & concurrency handling:
- For concurrency tests we will use a controlled client to maintain target concurrency (12 steady backpressure, bursts simulated to 30 for 60s intervals).
- Batching behavior noted: Redwood's runtime uses dynamic batching; we will provide batch size distributions so you can correlate batch size -> latency.

Reproducibility:
- Harness includes a locked seed for any nondeterministic ops and an environment file (env.sample) that pins model version, quantization profile, hardware type (e.g., A100-80GB) and runtime config.
- We'll publish the exact container SHA and the runner commit ID used for the run.

Next: Can you confirm the model family you want pinned for the pilot and whether you want us to also test a quantized variant? Also confirming Tue 2026-03-02 10:00 PT works for a 30-min kickoff.

—Dylan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
